title: About Hamza Khan
seoDescription: The story and communication philosophy of Hamza Khan — professional speaker, workshop facilitator, and communication coach.

intro.heading: The Story Behind Move Before You Know
intro.introduction: I am a professional speaker and communication coach. My journey to the stage was not a straight line, but a series of unpredictable pivots that taught me the true value of clear communication under pressure.

portrait.url: /media/Startup Event Portrait with Trophy and Microphone.png

chapters.subtitle: Before the stages.
chapters.heading: When your world feels small, learning to speak reaches beyond it.
chapters.body:
I grew up in Kashmir and spent a lot of my early life focused on academics.

There were stretches when the world outside felt distant, and I spent a lot of time with my own thoughts — writing, thinking, and trying to understand what I wanted from life.

But whenever I had the chance to speak, I took it.

I debated. I presented in class. I spoke at school assemblies.

I was nervous. I was insecure about my English. But I loved the feeling of having something to say and being heard.

Speaking gave me something academics alone didn’t.

It made me feel visible, useful and connected to people.

Looking back, I think that is where my relationship with communication began.

When your world feels small, learning how to express yourself can become a way to reach beyond it.

image.alt: Hamza Khan in earlier speaking reflections

chapters.subtitle: When the door closes twice.
chapters.heading: You can't choose your starting point. But you can choose your next move.
chapters.body:
When one of my biggest dreams was simply to see more of the world.

I was accepted to a university in the United States, but I couldn’t afford the tuition.

So I looked elsewhere and eventually applied to study in Türkiye.

My visa was rejected.

I applied again.

Rejected again.

I still remember my sister coming into my room one morning to tell me about that second rejection.

At that moment, it felt much bigger than a visa.

I started wondering whether my circumstances were deciding the rest of my life for me.

Looking back, I had made one major mistake:

I had mistaken my starting point for my future.

I couldn’t choose where I was born.

I couldn’t control every financial circumstance.

And I couldn’t guarantee where life would eventually take me.

But I could still choose my next move.

So I applied a third time.

This time, I got through.

Years later, that experience became the foundation of Move Before You Know:

“You don’t choose your starting point. You can’t guarantee your destination. But you can choose your direction.”

chapters.subtitle: Learning to be heard.
chapters.heading: Confidence grows from repeated evidence that you can do the thing.
chapters.body:
Moving to Türkiye opened doors I couldn’t have predicted.

But speaking itself wasn’t new to me. I had loved it for years.

What changed was that I started treating communication as a craft.

I recorded myself.

I entered competitions.

I asked for feedback.

I studied speakers I admired.

I reached out to people who were far better than me and asked them to teach me.

Whenever I felt stuck, I kept returning to one question:

What can I do next?

Over time, something I had loved instinctively became something I practised deliberately.

That process eventually took me into competitive speaking, international speaking opportunities and, in 2025, becoming a Toastmasters Division Champion in Türkiye.

I learned that confidence rarely comes before action. It grows from repeated evidence that you can do the thing.

image.alt: 2025 Toastmasters Division Champion Türkiye Award Plaque

chapters.subtitle: Helping other people find their voice.
chapters.heading: Turning what you know into opportunities.
chapters.body:
As I improved, people started asking me for help with their own communication.

How do I structure this?

How do I stop rambling?

How do I sound more confident?

How do I explain something complicated simply?

How do I speak when the pressure is high?

And I began recognizing something familiar in the people I worked with.

They often knew more than they were able to communicate.

They had something valuable to say, but they weren’t always able to make other people see it yet.

I knew that feeling.

I know what it feels like to have something to say and struggle to express it.

That is when communication became more than something I wanted to master for myself.

I wanted to help other people become clearer, more confident and better able to turn what they know into opportunities.

chapters.subtitle: Communication with purpose.
chapters.heading: Move before you know.
chapters.body:
Today, I speak, facilitate workshops and coach people who need to communicate when it matters.

The format changes.

The belief underneath it doesn’t.

People shouldn’t miss opportunities simply because they haven’t yet learned how to communicate what they know, who they are or what they can contribute.

That is the work I care about.

Helping people find clarity.

Helping them build confidence through practice.

Helping them communicate what they know in a way other people can understand, trust and act on.

And when the road ahead is uncertain, I still come back to the same question that changed my own life:

What can I do next?

You don’t need to know exactly where the next step will lead.

Sometimes you simply have to—

Move before you know.
